speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you've had a tympanoplasty; were you trying to wear earrings immediately after surgery, or has this difficulty persisted for some time?

How would you describe the "shooting" ear pain exactly—is it sharp and sudden, or does it have a burning quality?

Have you noticed any drainage, fluid coming out of the ear, or a feeling of fullness since the operation?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy (to examine the eardrum and surgical graft).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Otoscopy pending; clinical findings include right postauricular tenderness elicited by tapping, which correlates with tenderness in the right tonsillar area, and a history of 20 decibel hearing improvement post-tympanoplasty one week ago. No drainage, fluid, or persistent fullness reported in current dialogue.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the clarification; pain triggered specifically by eating suggests nerve irritation rather than active tuberculosis. Given your history of tympanoplasty, could you tell me if you have noticed any changes in your hearing or a sensation of pressure in the ear?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry and Tympanometry to assess hearing and middle ear pressure.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Audiometry and Tympanometry pending; recent audiology report from one week ago indicates improved hearing by 20 decibels post-tympanoplasty. Clinical examination notes right postauricular tenderness elicited by tapping, correlating with tenderness in the right tonsillar area. No drainage, fluid, or persistent fullness reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That right postauricular and tonsillar tenderness is highly concerning for Gradenigo's syndrome, which involves petrositis (inflammation of the petrous bone) often following ear surgery. Could you tell me if you have experienced any pain behind your eye or any double vision in that right eye?

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI of the petrous temporal bone.

REQUEST TEST: CT Temporal Bone to rule out mastoiditis or osteomyelitis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No pain behind the eye or double vision reported; patient reports occasional shooting ear pain with eating and discomfort wearing earrings. Pending MRI of the petrous temporal bone and CT Temporal Bone per request.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (triggered by eating) with post-tympanoplasty scarring/contracture causing mechanical discomfort with earrings. Gradenigo's syndrome is unlikely given the absence of retro-orbital pain, diplopia, and fever.

The shooting pain with chewing points to nerve irritation, while the ear piercing issue suggests fibrosis at the graft site rather than active infection or tuberculosis. Do you have a history of diabetes or any other neurological conditions that might predispose you to neuropathic pain?
